questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: Two thin concentric conducting spherical shells in [Electrostatics] have radii $R_1$ and $R_2 = 2R_1$. The inner shell has charge $Q = +3\,\mu\text{C}$ and the outer shell is earthed. What is the electrostatic potential of the inner shell?
questions.solution: Since outer shell is earthed, its potential is zero: $V_2 = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac{Q}{R_2} + \frac{Q'}{R_2}\right) = 0 \implies Q' = -Q$. Potential of inner shell is $V_1 = \frac{1}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac{Q}{R_1} + \frac{Q'}{R_2}\right) = \frac{Q}{4\pi\varepsilon_0}\left(\frac{1}{R_1} - \frac{1}{2R_1}\right) = \frac{Q(1)}{4\pi\varepsilon_0 2 R_1}$.
questions.explanation: Analyze the physical model and equations in Electrostatics.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question: One mole of ideal gas undergoes a polytropic expansion $P V^2 = C$ in [Electrostatics] from volume $V_0 = 1\text{ m}^3$ at pressure $P_0 = 10^5\text{ Pa}$ to $V_1 = 2\text{ m}^3$. Calculate the magnitude of work done by the gas in $\text{kJ}$ rounded to nearest integer.
questions.solution: Work done in polytropic process with $n=2$: $W = \frac{P_0 V_0 - P_1 V_1}{n - 1} = P_0 V_0 \left(1 - \frac{V_0}{V_1}\right) = 10^5 \times 1 \times (1 - 0.5) = 5 \times 10^4\text{ J} = 50\text{ kJ}$.
questions.explanation: Calculate using quantitative physical laws in Electrostatics.
